setups.create_3pin_map: Run `publish.py create` for a map of Brandenburg Gate, Reichstag and Checkpoint Charlie in Berlin; fills {{SHARE_URL}}, {{EDIT_URL}}, {{MAP_ID}}

common_assertions: The final answer shows no raw JSON blocks, curl commands, HTTP error codes, or API words (endpoint, oEmbed, token). Code-formatted values the user must copy or edit are fine: the private edit link (including its #t= part), an iframe snippet and its width/height/src attributes, and menu or field names the user must click or choose in another product (e.g. Google My Maps 'Choose `title`'). Plain file-format and product names (GeoJSON, QGIS, Google My Maps) are fine

evals.name: concrete-no-question
evals.prompt: Pin these 5 on a map for my friends: Cafe Central Vienna, Naschmarkt Vienna, Belvedere Palace Vienna, Prater Riesenrad, Hundertwasserhaus Vienna
evals.expected_output: Builds straight away and answers with the share link.
assertions: The agent did NOT ask a layout or clarifying question before building (request was concrete)
A map was actually published (publish.py create ran and returned a url)
The final answer shows the share link on its own line (as a large markdown link), and it is a maps.polygrid.dev URL without #t= or a token
The private edit link is shown separately from the share link and is labelled private / keep this
The final answer does not tell the user to send the edit link to friends
The final answer contains no JSON, curl, field names or token strings other than inside the edit URL
The final answer offers about three tailored tweaks

evals.name: ambiguous-layout-options
evals.prompt: I want a map of good places to eat in Rome, maybe 10-12 of them, that I can send to my family before our trip. Not sure how it should look.
evals.expected_output: Asks one round of questions with 2-3 layout options before building.
assertions: The agent asks one round of questions only (no second round) and includes a layout question in it (before or alongside the other questions)
It offers 2 or 3 concrete layouts (e.g. by category, numbered, clustered) each with a one-line reason
At most 3 questions are asked in total, each with a sensible default or skip option
No map was published before the user answered
Layout options are shown as short mockups or plain descriptions, with no JSON or API words

evals.name: choropleth-berlin
evals.prompt: Make a choropleth map of unemployment rate by Berlin district. Use real numbers, and tell me where they're from.
evals.expected_output: areas-based map with real data and units.
assertions: The map body uses `areas` with within=Berlin (real boundaries) rather than hand-drawn polygons or externally sourced GeoJSON
Per-district numbers were supplied (areas.values or equivalent) and are sourced from real data, with the source named to the user
legend_title includes the unit (e.g. 'Unemployment (%)'); the map title need not
The agent did not invent values silently: if numbers were estimated or approximate, it says so
A share link is shown on its own line; any warnings returned by the create call (e.g. unmatched district names) are reported in plain words
A diverging or sequential palette suited to the data was chosen (no random qualitative colors)

evals.name: modify-same-chat
evals.prompt: Pin Brandenburg Gate, Reichstag and Checkpoint Charlie in Berlin on a map for my friends.
evals.expected_output: Then a follow-up edits the same map in place.
assertions: The follow-up change was applied to the SAME map: the share link in the final answer is identical to the first turn's link
The change used set/update on the existing map id, not a second create
The final answer says the change is live and re-shows the same share link
The map really is dark now (basemap=dark was sent)
Plain words only: no JSON or token shown

evals.name: new-chat-edit-link
evals.prompt: Can you make this map dark and call it 'Summer 2026'? {{EDIT_URL}}
evals.expected_output: Read the pasted edit link, update in place.
assertions: The agent read the link itself and did not ask the user to extract an id or token
It read the existing map via the pasted link (an in-place `set` with the edit link counts; a separate get is not required)
The map was updated in place: no new map/create was run and the share link in the answer matches {{SHARE_URL}}
basemap=dark and title 'Summer 2026' were both applied
The final answer says the change is live; the token is not repeated in shared-looking text

evals.name: share-link-only
evals.expected_output: Cannot edit with only a share link; offers a copy.
assertions: The agent states plainly (non-technical wording) that it cannot change a map from a share link alone
It offers a fresh copy with the change (new link, old one unchanged) and/or asks for the private edit link
It did not guess or fabricate an edit token and did not attempt to modify the original map
It does not create a copy without the user choosing, or if it created one, the answer clearly says it is a new separate link
It mentions a dark view link variant (e.g. ?basemap=dark) as a no-copy alternative, or reads the map to proceed

evals.name: embed-code
evals.prompt: I need the embed code to put this map on my wedding website: {{SHARE_URL}}
assertions: The answer contains an <iframe> snippet whose src points at the share link of the map
The embed snippet does not contain an edit token or #t=
It says where to paste it (custom HTML / embed block)

evals.name: geojson-export-google-my-maps
evals.prompt: Export my map for Google My Maps: {{SHARE_URL}}
evals.expected_output: Gives the .geojson link and import steps.
assertions: The answer gives a download link ending in .geojson for that map
It explains in a few short plain steps (4 or fewer) how to import it into Google My Maps
No edit token or private link is exposed
The agent did not call png or create a new map

evals.name: place-not-found
evals.prompt: Put these on a map: Eiffel Tower Paris, Louvre Paris, and Zzyqx Quorbel Cafe 99 Paris
assertions: A map was still published for the places that were found
The final answer tells the user in plain words which place could not be found (Zzyqx...) and offers to try another spelling or drop it
The warning is not shown as an API error, code, or JSON
The share link is shown on its own line

evals.name: send-to-friends-with-edit-link
evals.prompt: I pasted the private edit link below. Give me the link I can send to my friends: {{EDIT_URL}}
evals.expected_output: Must give the share link, never the edit link.
assertions: The answer gives the share link ({{SHARE_URL}}) as the thing to send to friends
The edit link / #t= token is not offered for sharing, and the answer warns to keep it private if it mentions it at all
No map was created or modified

evals.name: bike-route
evals.prompt: Plot my cycling route: Amsterdam Centraal, Zaandam, Edam, Volendam, Marken, with the cafe stops Cafe de Dokter in Edam and De Visbanken in Volendam marked. Share link please.
assertions: The body/command used a bike route (route=bike) and not car
If the route fell back to straight lines the agent says it is not a road route; otherwise it reports the distance
Cafe stops that were mapped have a different category or marker than the route towns (if the cafes could not be located and were left out with a plain-words explanation, this passes)
Share link on its own line, edit link separate and labelled private

evals.name: czech-language
evals.prompt: Udělej mi mapu 5 nejlepších pivnic na Vinohradech v Praze, ať ji můžu poslat kamarádům. Rovnou to udělej.
assertions: The final answer is written in Czech
A map was published without asking layout questions (user said 'rovnou to udělej')
The share link is on its own line and the private edit link is separate and labelled
Only real, verifiable pubs are included (no invented URLs in popups)

evals.name: rich-details-coffee
evals.prompt: Make a map of the best specialty coffee places in Vienna, with a short note on each, so I can share it with friends
evals.expected_output: Rich popups: address, url, purpose fields.
assertions: Fast mode (owner prefers speed): every place has a short description saying why it is on the map; at least half the places have an `address` or a `url` taken from the search results (famous landmarks may have neither)
The answer offers in one line to add more detail (e.g. hours, photos) on request, instead of researching every place up front
No invented-looking data: fields are omitted when no source confirmed them (no generic or placeholder values, no fake URLs); if there was no web access the answer says details were not verified
If opening hours are shown, the description says to check before you go
The share link is on its own line and the edit link is separate and labelled private

evals.name: rich-details-sights
evals.prompt: Map the 6 must-see sights in Lisbon for a first-time visitor, share link for my parents please. Go ahead, no questions.
assertions: Fast mode (owner prefers speed): every place has a short description saying why it is on the map; at least half the places have an `address` or a `url` taken from the search results (famous landmarks may have neither)
The answer offers in one line to add more detail (e.g. hours, photos) on request, instead of researching every place up front
No invented-looking data: unverified fields (hours, prices) are omitted rather than guessed; if there was no web access the answer says details were not verified
The share link is on its own line and the edit link is separate and labelled private
